newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police arrest Gucci ex-wife in murder plot.
newsitem.headline: Italian police arrest Gucci ex-wife in murder plot.

text.p: The gangland-style killing of fashion heir Maurizio Gucci took a dramatic twist on Friday when police arrested the businessman's ex-wife on suspicion of ordering the fatal shooting two years ago.

A police official said Patrizia Reggiani Martinelli, 49, had been arrested in an apartment in central Milan on Friday morning. Another woman and three men were also detained separately in connection with the March 1995 shooting.
"We confirm that we arrested Patrizia Reggiani Martinelli this morning on suspicion of involvement in the killing," a police official told Reuters.
The arrest swoop was carried out on the orders of Milan prosecutor Carlo Nocerino who has been leading the inquiry into one of Italy's most mysterious recent crimes.
It was another gripping chapter in a long saga of bitter feuds and ugly power struggles behind the family's chic image.

According to legal sources, investigators allege that Gucci's elegant dark-haired ex-wife, with whom he had an acrimonious relationship, had commissioned the fatal attack. The couple had two children and reportedly squabbled over alimony.
Italian media, quoting judicial sources, said she allegedly paid more than half a billion lire ($300,000) to hire hit-men.
Gucci, 45, was shot dead in broad daylight outside his office in central Milan by a well-dressed assassin who pumped four shots into him from close range before climbing into a waiting getaway car.
Police confirmed Italian news reports which identified the other woman arrested as Giuseppina Auriemma, 51, a "spiritual adviser" of Gucci's ex-wife. She was arrested in Naples.

One of the men was Ivano Savioni, 40, a hotel concierge. The other two, whom police allege carried out the shooting, were named as Orazio Cicala, 58, who is in jail on drugs charges, and Benedetto Ceraulo, 35, who also has a previous criminal record.
Italy was awash with speculation that murky financial deals, battles for inheritance and boiling soap opera-style passions were all at play in the millionaire's murder.

The Gucci empire, with its unmistakable red and green motif and intertwined gilt GG logo, grew from a humble saddlery shop in Florence in 1906 into purveyors of luxury leather, luggage, shoes, ties and couture to the rich and famous.
Their clients ranged from film stars like Elizabeth Taylor and Grace Kelly to many of the world's leading statesmen and industrialists.
Gucci's style was a hallmark of casual elegance but came to symbolise 1980s brash consumer excesses after rapid expansion slapped is famous logo on thousands of franchised products.
Maurizio, the last grandson of founder Guccio Gucci, was plunged into feuds in the style of the Medicis of mediaeval Florence after inheriting his father's 50 percent share.
In one battle, Maurizio was convicted of attempted fraud after relatives accused him of forging his father's signature to evade inheritance tax. The conviction was later quashed.
Maurizo sold his 50 percent stake to Arab investment bank Investcorp for a reported $150-200 million in 1993 and stepped down as chairman. Investcorp had bought out his cousins in 1987.
Gucci has climbed back to financial health from big debts and losses and its shares are traded in Amsterdam and New York.
